rows.description: C4 duplicate invoice — same vendor, same amount, 28 days apart
rows.exception_summary: Duplicate invoice detected for vendor Acme Supplies: INV-2024-089 matches INV-2024-072, same amount EUR 12,450, 28 days apart, same line items.
rows.recommended_action: PROPOSE that the AP team review the flagged invoices INV-2024-089 and INV-2024-072, verify the duplicate criteria per Section 4.1, and if confirmed as a duplicate, void the duplicate invoice and maintain the block. If the invoices are deemed legitimate, require documented business justification and have a different authorized individual release the payment block to satisfy segregation‑of‑duties per Section 4.2. Record the outcome in the AP audit trail.
rows.limitations: This finding is an anomaly flag based on matching invoice data and policy criteria; it does not constitute definitive proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C1 three-way match violation — invoice EUR 500 above PO+GR
rows.exception_summary: Invoice EUR 18,500 exceeds PO EUR 18,000 by EUR 500 (3.3%), surpassing the allowed tolerance of 3% or EUR 150.
rows.recommended_action: Flag the invoice for AP Manager review; require justification for the variance, adjust the PO or obtain a credit note, and ensure the automatic payment block is resolved before clearing the invoice.
rows.limitations: This flag is based on a tolerance breach; it does not constitute evidence of fraud or misconduct. Anomaly flag, not proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C3 approval-threshold splitting — two invoices from same vendor totalling $19,800 within 7 days
rows.exception_summary: Two invoices (INV-2024-301 EUR 9,900 and INV-2024-302 EUR 9,850) submitted by the same requester to Office Depot within 7 days have a combined value of EUR 19,750, exceeding the $10,000 secondary‑approval threshold and matching the splitting indicators in policy.
rows.recommended_action: AP Manager should review the two invoices for possible splitting, verify requester intent, and if splitting is confirmed, escalate to Internal Audit within 2 business days as required. Consider applying a payment block pending investigation and ensure proper secondary‑approval is obtained for the cumulative amount.
rows.limitations: This is an anomaly flag based on matching policy indicators; it does not constitute definitive proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C5 SoD violation — AP Clerk who created invoice also removed payment block
rows.exception_summary: User JSMITH, who recorded the invoice, removed the payment block on invoice INV-2024-188, constituting an SOD-04 segregation‑of‑duties violation.
rows.recommended_action: 1. Conduct a human review to confirm JSMITH’s role (likely AP Clerk) and that no AP Supervisor/Manager approval was obtained. 2. Require documented justification for the removal, if any, and verify it meets Section 5.3. 3. Re‑assign removal authority to an authorized AP Supervisor or AP Manager for this transaction. 4. Update role‑based access controls to prevent future SOD‑04 breaches. 5. If staffing constraints exist, ensure compensating controls per Section 6 (monthly management review, automated violation reporting) are fully operational.
rows.limitations: This finding is an anomaly flag based on the provided evidence; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct without further investigation.

rows.description: C6 Benford's law anomaly — leading digit 9 at 41% vs expected 4.6%
rows.exception_summary: Benford's Law screening for FastPrint Ltd in Q3 shows the leading digit 9 in 41% of 14 invoices (expected 4.6%), triggering a medium‑severity anomaly flag with an estimated exposure of EUR 8,300.
rows.recommended_action: PROPOSAL: Initiate a manual review by Internal Audit. Expand the sample size beyond the 14 invoices, recalculate the Benford distribution, and cross‑check for duplicate invoices per Section 4.1. If anomalies persist, consider applying payment blocks per Section 5.1 while the investigation is ongoing.
rows.limitations: The Benford flag is an anomaly indicator only; it does not prove fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C2 invoice before goods receipt — invoice posted 5 days before GR
rows.exception_summary: Invoice INV-2024-355 was recorded on 2024-08-01, five days before the Goods Receipt was recorded on 2024-08-06 for vendor Nordic Steel, exposing EUR 22,000. This constitutes a three-way‑match exception per policy.
rows.recommended_action: Place a payment block on INV-2024-355 if not already applied, require AP Manager review and documented business justification, verify that a valid PO exists and that the PO amount aligns with the invoice, and confirm that the block is removed only after independent approval per SOD‑04 and SOD‑05.
rows.limitations: This flag reflects a policy deviation based on the available data; it does not constitute evidence of fraud or misconduct. Anomaly flag, not proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C1 + C4 compound — both three-way match violation and duplicate flag on same vendor
rows.exception_summary: Two high‑severity anomalies were identified for Meridian Consulting: (1) Invoice INV‑2024‑500 shows a variance of EUR 750 exceeding the three‑way‑match tolerance; (2) INV‑2024‑500 matches INV‑2024‑488 for the same vendor, amount EUR 15,000 and within 12 days, indicating a potential duplicate.
rows.recommended_action: Propose that AP management review both invoices: verify the purchase order and goods receipt for INV‑2024‑500, confirm that the EUR 750 variance exceeds the allowed tolerance and apply a payment block pending justification; for the duplicate case, confirm that INV‑2024‑488 and INV‑2024‑500 are indeed the same invoice, retain the duplicate alert, block payment on one invoice, and document the resolution. Document findings and obtain manager sign‑off before any payment.
rows.limitations: These findings are anomaly flags based on the available data; they do not constitute definitive evidence of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C4 duplicate — within EUR 1 tolerance; low exposure
rows.exception_summary: A low‑severity duplicate invoice alert was triggered for vendor Stationery World. Two invoices (INV-2024-601 for EUR 420.00 and INV-2024-598 for EUR 420.50) differ by EUR 0.50, which is within the EUR 1 tolerance, and the system auto‑blocked payment.
rows.recommended_action: AP team should review the two invoices, verify vendor number, amount tolerance, and invoice dates. If confirmed as a duplicate, void the duplicate invoice and maintain the block. If deemed a legitimate separate invoice, document the business justification, ensure a different reviewer releases the block to satisfy segregation‑of‑duties, and then clear the payment.
rows.limitations: This finding is an anomaly flag based on policy criteria and system detection; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C5 SoD + C3 threshold splitting — compound exception with critical severity
rows.exception_summary: AP Clerk RBROWN removed the payment block on invoice INV-2024-700 that they created (SOD-04 violation) and two invoices from Alpha Corp (EUR 14,200 and EUR 13,800) were issued by the same requester RBROWN within 6 days, indicating possible splitting to bypass the $10,000 secondary‑approval threshold.
rows.recommended_action: Propose that Internal Audit be engaged to review the RBROWN actions, verify whether any Finance Director written approval existed for the block removal, assess the two invoices for splitting, require the AP Manager to document a justification or corrective action, and consider re‑assigning RBROWN’s roles or obtaining Finance Director approval for any role consolidation. Update HR role records and reinforce training on SOD and splitting policies.
rows.limitations: This flag is based on detected anomalies in the data evidence and policy references; it does not constitute definitive proof of fraud or misconduct. Anomaly flag, not proof of fraud or misconduct.
